title: Bunyavirus Infections (Hantavirus, CCHF, Rift Valley Fever)

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man was brought in by ambulance with severe shortness of breath. He required immediate intubation for profound hypoxemia despite high flow oxygen. A collateral history was obtained from his brother. The patient came back from a trip to Colorado 2 weeks earlier where he helped his cousin renovate and clean an old farmhouse infested with rodents, cockroaches, and termites. The patient had tried drinking milk freshly squeezed from his cousin’s cow a few times. His symptoms began a few days after coming back from the trip with flu-like symptoms that rapidly progressed to a dry cough and severe dyspnea. His vital signs upon arrival were: temperature 39.1°C, blood pressure 60/40 mmHg, heart rate 120 beats/minute, and respiratory rate 30 breaths/minute. Labs: Total white cell count 15 ×109/L (60% neutrophil with a significant amount of immature cells, 15% lymphocytes with a significant amount of atypical cells) Hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL (hematocrit 64%) Platelet count 62,000/μL AST 24 U/L ALT 25 U/L Bilirubin 1 mg/dL eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73 m2 Chest X-ray:
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely cause of his infection?
questions.explanation: Hantavirus The clinical picture of a rapidly progressing respiratory failure associated with diffuse pulmonary edema, fever, leukocytosis with left shift and atypical lymphocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and elevated hematocrit, in the correct epidemiologic setting (Utah, Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico) and exposure history (rodents), is consistent with hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (Sin Nombre virus). (Image from Shandro JR, Jauregui JM. Wildernessacquired zoonoses. In Auerbach PS, Cushing TA, Harris NS, eds. Auerbach’s Wilderness Medicine. 7th ed. Elsevier; 2017.)

questions.question: A 14-year old boy was cleaning out an old cottage in Saskatchewan, then developed fever, myalgias, arthralgias, nausea and vomiting. He then presented to the ER with rapidly developing respiratory distress.

parts.text: What is the most likely virus?
What family does it belong to?
What is the animal reservoir for it?

questions.model_answer:
a) Most likely virus: Sin Nombre virus.
b) Family: Hantaviridae (order Bunyavirales).
c) Animal reservoir: deer mouse (Peromyscus maniculatus).
d) Syndrome: Hantavirus (cardio)pulmonary syndrome.
e) Transmission: inhalation of aerosolized virus from rodent urine, feces, or saliva, typically when disturbing dust in enclosed spaces (e.g., cleaning out an old cabin/cottage) contaminated by infected rodent excreta.

parts.text: 2 Hantaviruses (table to fill in vector, clinical manifestation, tx etc.)

cohort_answer.text: Sin Nombre virus - deer mice - HPS (Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome). Seoul virus - pet rats (aka Norway rat aka Rattus norvegicus) - HFRS (Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome). Puumala virus - bank voles (high yield factoid) - HFRS. Reference: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/hantaviruses

questions.question: PM 2. Young kid who cleaned out a farmhouse in Moose Jaw, develops a febrile illness with severe respiratory symptoms

parts.text: What is the most likely diagnosis (1)
What family does this virus belong to (1)
What is the mode of transmission (1)

cohort_answer.text: Hantavirus Pulmonary syndrome. Family: Bunyaviridae. Vector: Rodent/Deer mouse. Transmission: Inhalation of aerosolized feces. Management: Supportive care, Ribavirin in HFRS not in HPS.

questions.question: Case of hanta pulmonary syndrome in Saskatchewan

parts.text: What is your modality of treatment?

questions.model_answer:
a) Virus: Sin Nombre virus.
b) Family: Hantaviridae.
c) Treatment: supportive care only (ICU-level management, mechanical ventilation, and in severe cases extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for cardiopulmonary support) - there is no proven specific antiviral for hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (ribavirin has shown benefit for Old World hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome but not for HPS).

questions.question: Q20 (2017 PM). Pulmonary syndrome from Saskatchewan

parts.text: What is the name of the virus?

cohort_answer.text: Sin Nombre virus. Canada reports 10-15% of North American cases (0-13 yearly); main pathogen in western provinces (one Quebec case); spring/early summer; inhalation of excreta (urine mainly, also feces/saliva) from infected deer mice (Peromyscus maniculatus); 30% mortality; incubation 9-33 (up to 51) days, typical 14-17d; 4 phases (febrile prodrome, cardiopulmonary, diuretic, convalescent); bilateral edema mimics ARDS, low platelets, high HCT common; diagnosis via serology, PCR. Family: Hantavirus, Order Bunyavirales. Treatment: Supportive; careful fluid administration; ventilatory support +/- ECMO; no efficacy for ribavirin.

parts.text: Fill in the table for Hantaan virus and other hantaviruses: Vector/Host, Geo distribution, Clinical manifestations, Diagnosis, Treatment.

cohort_answer.text:
Hantaan virus | Striped field mouse (agriculture) - transmission via aerosolized rodent excrement | Korea, China, Eastern Russia | Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), especially in fall and spring and relating to agriculture | Immunologic - ELISA for viral IgM in blood/CSF, but also RT-PCR from blood/tissue | Ribavirin effective for severe - reduction in mortality seen in one study, other studies did not confirm
Sin Nombre virus | Deer mouse, other rodents - transmission via aerosolized rodent excrement | North America/South America | Pulmonary syndrome; Fever, shock, pulmonary edema | Same as above | Supportive care, avoid excess fluid administration. Ribavirin not shown to be effective

questions.question: For each virus, what is the animal reservoir?

cohort_answer.text: Herpes B: Macaque monkey. Sin Nombre virus: Deer mouse/rat. Rabies: Bats and raccoons. Chlamydia psittaci: Parrots.

questions.question: Q66 (2004 AM). 3 rare diseases in Canada - list the provinces in which they are found: Hydatid disease; Lyme disease; Hantavirus

parts.text: List the provinces where each disease is found

cohort_answer.text: Hydatid disease - Alberta, northern Ontario (E. multilocularis). Lyme disease - Ontario, Manitoba, Quebec, NB, NS. Hantavirus - Saskatchewan.
